questions.q: Why should you read a posting's responsibilities rather than relying on its title?
options: Titles are legally standardized so responsibilities never matter
Titles are company-specific labels; two postings with the same title can describe very different work
Responsibilities are always identical across companies
Titles are never listed in postings
questions.explain: The same title can mean a reporting seat in one company and a BI-developer seat in another, so the responsibilities tell you what the job really is.

questions.q: Which of these is a title the lesson suggests searching in addition to Salesforce-branded titles?
questions.explain: Sales Operations, RevOps, Business Systems, CRM, and Reporting Analyst roles often use the same skills under non-Salesforce titles.

questions.q: In the three-bucket posting method, which bucket includes phrases introduced by 'preferred' or 'a plus'?
questions.explain: Skills flagged as preferred or a plus are nice-to-haves; few candidates match every one, so they should not stop you from applying.

questions.q: Which title's work product is mainly the data pipeline and model (often Snowflake, dbt, Git) rather than the dashboard?
questions.explain: Analytics Engineers focus on reliable, reusable pipelines and models; dashboards are downstream of that work.

questions.q: A posting lists 'strong SOQL and data quality skills.' Which earlier course maps most directly to that keyword?
questions.explain: SOQL and data-quality work is covered by the SOQL & Salesforce Data Management course.
